subject: Maths
title: Expanding single brackets
subtitle: Algebraic Expressions · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can expand single brackets by multiplying every term inside by the term outside.

key_vocab.definition: Expanding means removing the brackets by multiplying every term inside by the term outside.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can expand single brackets by multiplying every term inside by the term outside.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Expanding -- Expanding means removing the brackets by multiplying every term inside by the term outside.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply the term outside by EVERY term inside. Watch the signs carefully when there's a negative outside.
3(x + 2) = 3x + 6
Multiply both terms

Key examples:
  ✓ 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6  (both terms)
  ✓ −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10  (watch signs)
  ✓ x(x + 3) = x² + 3x  (x × x = x²)
  ✗ 3(x + 2) = 3x + 2  (missed second term)
  ✗ −2(x + 3) = −2x + 6  (should be −6)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – all positive
  Expand 3(x + 4)
  3 × x = 3x
  3 × 4 = 12
  Combine: 3x + 12
  = 3x + 12
  (Multiply each term inside by 3.)

Example 2 – with subtraction
  Expand 5(x − 2)
  5 × x = 5x
  5 × (−2) = −10
  Combine: 5x − 10
  = 5x − 10
  (The minus sign belongs to the 2.)

sections.title: With subtraction inside
sections.content:
The minus sign stays with its term.

(a) 3(x − 4)
(b) 6(x − 1)
(c) 8(x − 5)
(d) 9(x − 2)

sections.title: Mixed expand and simplify
sections.content:
Expand, then collect any like terms.

(a) 3(x + 2) + 4
(b) 5(x − 1) + 2x
(c) 2(x + 3) + 3(x − 1)
(d) x(x + 2) − x
(e) −2(x − 4) + 5
